issues.legal_issue: An uncompleted government works contract, including contractual obligations to correct defective or unfinished work, subsists for the purpose of candidate disqualification.
material_facts: The candidate was a partner in a firm holding government contracts to construct a road and a dispensary building.
When nominations were filed, items required by both contracts remained unfinished, including road boundary and milestone markers and parts of the building work.
The contracts also required the contractor to repair defective work during specified periods.
Earlier certificates stating that the work was complete were later contradicted by certificates and evidence that work remained to be done.
issues.conclusion: The contracts had not been fully performed and subsisted when nominations were filed, so the disqualification applied.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a person is disqualified while a qualifying government contract subsists. The Explanation treats a contract fully performed by the candidate as not subsisting merely because the Government has not performed its part. Applying Chatturbhuj Vithaldas Jasani v. Moreshwar Parashram, a contractual obligation to correct or replace defective work remains part of the contract; execution is not complete until it is properly performed. Trivial defects may not prevent substantial completion, but the unfinished work here was not merely trivial.

rule.if: election_disqualification_case and government_work_contract and candidate_has_contract_interest and (material_work_unfinished or contractual_duty_to_correct_work)

predicates.election_disqualification_case: An election proceeding concerns whether a candidate was disqualified from standing for election.
predicates.government_work_contract: A contract with the government requires work to be executed for it.
predicates.candidate_has_contract_interest: The candidate has an interest in the government work contract.
predicates.material_work_unfinished: The contractor had not completed material work required by the contract.
predicates.contractual_duty_to_correct_work: The contract required the contractor to correct defective or improperly performed work.

issues.definition: If an election-disqualification proceeding concerns a candidate interested in a government work contract and material work remains unfinished or the contract requires correction of work, the candidate is disqualified.

issues.legal_issue: A partner in a firm holding a government contract has an interest in that contract sufficient to attract candidate disqualification.
material_facts: The government works contracts were held by a partnership firm.
The candidate was a partner in that firm when nominations were filed.
issues.conclusion: The candidate's status as a partner gave him a sufficient interest in the firm's government contracts for the disqualification to apply.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 applies where a candidate has an interest in a qualifying government contract; a partner in the firm holding the contract has an interest sufficient to attract the section.

predicates.election_disqualification_case: An election proceeding concerns whether a candidate was disqualified from standing for election.
predicates.government_contract_with_firm: A firm holds a contract with the government.
predicates.candidate_is_partner: The candidate is a partner in the firm holding the government contract.

issues.definition: If an election-disqualification proceeding concerns a candidate who is a partner in a firm holding a government contract, the candidate has a sufficient interest in that contract.

issues.legal_issue: A private dissolution of a contracting partnership does not end a candidate's connection with its government contract when the government has not been notified or accepted a substitute contractor.
material_facts: The candidate's partnership firm held the government contracts.
The firm was dissolved and its business was transferred to another person before the election.
The government was not notified of the dissolution and had not accepted the transferee in place of the firm.
issues.conclusion: The private dissolution did not release the candidate from the contractual relationship with the government or remove the disqualification.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate's interest in a subsisting government contract attracts disqualification. A private dissolution cannot by itself escape the candidate's liability under the contract; the Court found no novation where the government had not been notified and had not accepted the proposed substitute. The judgment also relied on Chatturbhuj Vithaldas Jasani v. Moreshwar Parashram.

rule.if: election_disqualification_case and candidate_is_partner_in_contracting_firm and partnership_dissolved and government_not_notified and government_not_accepted_substitute

predicates.election_disqualification_case: An election proceeding concerns whether a candidate was disqualified from standing for election.
predicates.candidate_is_partner_in_contracting_firm: The candidate was a partner in the firm holding the government contract.
predicates.partnership_dissolved: The partnership holding the contract was privately dissolved.
predicates.government_not_notified: The government was not notified of the partnership's dissolution.
predicates.government_not_accepted_substitute: The government did not accept the person taking over the business as a substitute contractor.

issues.definition: If a candidate connected to a contracting firm is involved in an election-disqualification proceeding and the firm is privately dissolved without notice to or acceptance by the government of a substitute, the candidate remains connected to the contract.

issues.legal_issue: The fact that a government works contract was signed by an officer other than the government secretary does not remove the contract from the candidate-disqualification rule.
material_facts: The contracts were with the government and were signed by an Executive Engineer rather than the Secretary to the Government.
The candidate relied on the identity of the signatory to argue that the disqualification did not apply.
issues.conclusion: The signatory argument did not avoid the disqualification.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Chatturbhuj Vithaldas Jasani v. Moreshwar Parashram, the Court rejected the argument based on Article 299 that the contracts had to be signed by the Secretary to the Government to attract the election-law disqualification under section 9A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

predicates.election_disqualification_case: An election proceeding concerns whether a candidate was disqualified from standing for election.
predicates.government_work_contract: A contract with the government requires work to be executed for it.
predicates.contract_signed_by_nonsecretary_officer: A government officer other than the government secretary signed the contract.

issues.definition: If an election-disqualification proceeding concerns a government work contract signed by an officer other than the government secretary, that signatory fact does not avoid disqualification.

issues.legal_issue: When the returned candidate is disqualified and no other candidate remains in the contest, the sole rival may be declared elected after the returned candidate's votes are treated as thrown away.
material_facts: The returned candidate had been disqualified because he was interested in subsisting government contracts.
Five of the seven original candidates withdrew, leaving only the returned candidate and the election petitioner to contest the seat.
The returned candidate received more votes than the election petitioner.
issues.conclusion: The Court declared the returned candidate's election void, treated the votes cast for him as thrown away, and declared the sole other contesting candidate elected.
issues.legal_principle: In the election appeal, the Court treated the returned candidate's votes as thrown away after finding his election void and declared the only other contesting candidate elected. The judgment does not identify a separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this consequential ruling.

predicates.election_appeal: An appeal concerns the result of an election.
predicates.returned_candidate_is_disqualified: The candidate declared elected is found to have been disqualified.
predicates.no_other_contesting_candidate: No candidate other than the returned candidate and the sole rival remains in the contest.

issues.definition: If an election appeal establishes that the returned candidate was disqualified and there was no other contesting candidate besides the sole rival, the sole rival is declared elected.
